domain_claim: Changing ForEach.input (input collection expression) in the YAML source MUST produce a different canonical_digest
notes: Currently ForEach.input is NOT hashed at all. The fix must inject hasher.update(input.as_bytes()) into the ForEach arm of digest_step_primitive. This seed requires proving that the post-fix code actually includes input in the hash computation. Suggests Kani for bounded proof of field coverage, proptest for random variation validation, fuzz for adversarial input edge cases.

domain_claim: Changing ForEach.at_once (max concurrency limit) MUST produce a different canonical_digest
notes: at_once is Option<u32>. The canonical representation decision: hash at_once.unwrap_or(1) as u32 le_bytes. This means None and Some(1) produce identical digest contributions (semantic equivalence). Kani should verify that variation in at_once values produces variation in digest. Proptest: random u32 values → digest uniqueness.

domain_claim: Changing ForEach.variable (loop variable name) MUST produce a different canonical_digest
notes: Variable names are YAML strings. The fix hashes them as raw bytes. Non-ASCII names (e.g., Unicode) are hashed byte-by-byte — this is correct and deterministic. Kani: bounded proof that variable.as_bytes() feeds hasher. Proptest: random variable names → digest uniqueness.

domain_claim: Changing any text content of any body step in ForEach.body MUST produce a different canonical_digest
model_boundary: canonical_digest() pure function in vb_compile; recursive descent through StepAst tree
notes: Body steps are Vec<StepAst>. Each body step contributes its step.id and calls digest_step_primitive recursively. Changing any field of any body step must change the digest. This is the deepest coverage gap — body content is completely unhashed. Kani: bounded proof that body steps contribute to hasher. Proptest: random body content → digest uniqueness.

domain_claim: canonical_digest remains deterministic after the ForEach fix: identical source always produces identical digest
notes: Existing determinism tests cover name-level differences. This seed targets post-fix determinism: ForEach field hashing must not introduce non-determinism (e.g., no random seed, no HashMap iteration, no timestamp). The fix adds only deterministic input: string bytes, integer bytes, recursive hashing. Kani: bounded proof of deterministic execution. Proptest: same source compiled 1000 times → same digest.

domain_claim: Both copies of canonical_digest (compile/mod.rs and part_05.rs) produce identical digests for identical input after the fix
notes: This is a high-risk seed because the two copies already have minor discrepancies (e.g., primitive naming: 'together' vs 'parallel'). The ForEach fix must be applied identically to both. Proptest: generate random WorkflowSource with ForEach steps, compile via both paths, assert digest equality. No Kani needed — this is a behavioral equivalence test.

domain_claim: Semantically equivalent ForEach inputs (at_once=None vs Some(1)) produce identical digest contributions
model_boundary: canonical_digest() pure function in vb_compile; at_once unwrap_or(1) resolution
notes: The lowering code (part_02.rs:172) resolves at_once.unwrap_or(1), making None and Some(1) semantically equivalent. The digest MUST reflect this equivalence by hashing the resolved value (1) not the Option tag. Kani: bounded proof that at_once=None and at_once=Some(1) produce identical hash input.

domain_claim: Non-ForEach primitives (Set, Finish) produce digests unchanged by the ForEach fix
model_boundary: canonical_digest() pure function in vb_compile; Set + Finish arms unchanged
notes: Regression guard. The ForEach fix adds a new match arm; existing Set and Finish hashing behavior must be unchanged. Proptest: generate random workflows with only Set and Finish steps, compile pre- and post-fix (or just verify behavior matches pre-fix expectations), assert digest equality.

domain_claim: digest_step_primitive is exhaustive for ForEach: all four source-level fields (variable, input, at_once, body) are hashed in canonical order with field delimiters
notes: The current catch-all pattern (other => hasher.update(name)) is a generalized hazard. The fix replaces it with an explicit ForEach arm. This seed requires proving that the ForEach arm actually hashes all four fields. Flux: refinement-type proof that no ForEach field is uninspected. Kani: bounded verification of field coverage. If the compiler (rustc) can enforce exhaustive field usage via match patterns, that is the strongest proof — but the ForEach variant has named fields, so destructuring in the match arm forces all fields to be mentioned. Using '{ variable, input, at_once, body }' in the match pattern makes field omission a compiler error.

domain_claim: ForEach field delimiting prevents boundary collisions: hasher absorbs delimited byte sequences where no valid YAML identifier value can create false boundaries
model_boundary: digest_step_primitive() ForEach arm; byte-level delimiter injection
notes: Without delimiters, hash('variable=ab' + 'input=c') == hash('variable=a' + 'input=bc'). The fix uses b':' as delimiter. Since YAML identifiers do not contain ':', and variable/input names are YAML identifiers, this delimiter is unambiguous. Kani: bounded proof that no valid ForEach field value can contain the delimiter byte. This is a low-risk seed — the delimiter choice is constrained by the domain (YAML identifiers).
